static_traits.name: Gu Wen
static_traits.family_status: Living with son, main caregiving and economic source comes from bakery operation
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with suppliers and customers are affected by anxiety; has a few close friends but has not yet revealed this fear to them
static_traits.medical_history: No notable physical illness; no similar psychological problems before, and no psychotherapy received
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly and fairly organized, able to engage in self-reflection and cooperation; emotionally tense but cooperative in attitude

basic_info.main_problem: I have always feared I will forget to turn off an oven at the bakery, causing a fire and destroying everything I worked hard to build.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because this fear has affected my ability to focus on running the business and brought marked stress and anxiety. I just want to stop being so anxious all the time.
growth_experiences: After becoming a single mother, the client alone undertook the responsibility of raising her son and opened a small bakery as the main source of livelihood; a few months after opening the shop, she began to fear that 'forgetting to turn off the oven will cause a fire'.
No previous similar anxiety problems or treatment history; overall physical health is good.

core_beliefs: Once I make a mistake, it will bring disastrous consequences
I must take full responsibility for all safety; there can be no oversight

special_situations.event: Checking equipment and ovens every day when closing after work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not achieve absolute foolproofness, I will very likely make a fatal mistake and ruin everything
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly checks the shutdown procedure, adds safety measures, and repeatedly rehearses the checking steps in the mind
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I may have forgotten to turn off an oven; if something happens the whole shop will burn down.

special_situations.event: On especially busy workdays with many tasks
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: When I am overwhelmed by tasks and can barely breathe, I will surely miss key details and cause a major disaster
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: More nervously monitors the self, increases checking frequency, and avoids distractions and interference from others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: With such a busy day today, I will most likely miss a shutdown step.

special_situations.event: Thinking about the bakery being the main source of support for oneself and one's son
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If anything goes wrong in the shop, I will be unable to support my son and we will lose everything
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Strictly controls safety and procedures, raises self-demands, and is unwilling to seek others' help
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If something goes wrong, my child's and my life will be over.

special_situations.event: At night after returning home, when preparing to sleep, recalls that day's shop-closing steps
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only by constantly worrying and repeatedly checking in my mind can I ensure nothing is missed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly replaying the shutdown scene in the mind, trying to maintain vigilance through worry
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: What if I really missed something?

core_conflict.wish: Longs to fully control and ensure safety, so as to be a reliable caregiver and provider
core_conflict.fear: Fearing that one lapse could cause disaster, loss of livelihood, and failing one's responsibility to the children
defense_goal: Suppresses anxiety through excessive checking and rational control, avoiding any possible mistake

object_relations.self_representation: A responsibility bearer/mother who needs to stay vigilant at all times and cannot make mistakes
object_relations.object_representation: Others may not understand my worries; the outside world is full of potential risks and uncontrollable factors

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor asks about 'the probability and evidence of the worst-case scenario occurring'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiences the counselor as downplaying risks and possibly not understanding the responsibility they bear (transference: projecting the worry about 'having one's responsibility slighted' onto the counselor)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a calm, restrained, data-based, and procedural tone, emphasizes responsibility and consequences, focuses on process and risk-management details, and reduces emotional language.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to consider seeking support from friends or expressing concerns
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worries that exposing vulnerability will be misunderstood or seem unprofessional, attributing their own unease to 'others will not understand' (transference: distrust of others' degree of understanding)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Restrained and cautious tone, uses vague expressions (for example 'they probably would not understand'), quickly returns to topics of self-pressure and responsibility, avoiding going deeply into personal vulnerability.

manifestations: As a shop owner and single mother, feels fully responsible for choices and outcomes; worries that a single oversight will lead to catastrophic consequences
Although having close friends, not sharing specific fears, tending to bear pressure alone
outcomes: The support system is not fully mobilized; anxiety is maintained or worsens
Interpersonal interaction with suppliers and customers is affected

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths.
manifestations: Self-demand 'must achieve absolute safety, cannot have any mistakes'
Maintaining control and a sense of security through strict rules

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Repeatedly checking oneself, constantly replaying the shutdown procedure in the mind
Highly sensitive to mistakes and self-reproaching

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Worrying friends will not understand one's fear, thus avoiding seeking help and expressing

exception_events.target_problem: After closing the shop or on busy workdays, the client is usually troubled by the worry that 'forgetting to turn off the oven will cause a fire', finding it hard to relax, affecting sleep and work focus.
exception_events.unique_outcome: On relatively leisurely workdays, the client more easily maintains a sense of control and order, with markedly reduced anxiety, and can leave relatively at ease after completing the checks according to procedure.
exception_events.reason: Clues: the task load was lower, the environment was quieter, and attention was more focused on the process itself, thus obtaining the subjective experience of a 'sense of control' and 'certainty'.

positive_force: Strong sense of responsibility, valuing safety and procedures
Has established and strengthened multiple safety measures and checking procedures
Has willingness to try new daily routines and cognitive restructuring
Has some social support (has close friends)
negative_force: Cognitive biases of catastrophizing and fortune telling are prominent
Low tolerance for uncertainty; a tendency toward all-or-nothing standards
Excessive self-monitoring and repeated checking maintain the anxiety cycle
Avoids seeking help for fear of being misunderstood; the support system is not mobilized
Disturbed sleep leads to a negative cycle of next-day anxiety and decreased efficiency

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated checking and ritualized confirmation when closing the shop, accompanied by strong worry
antecedent: Scenes of closing the shop, shutting down ovens and equipment
When workdays are especially busy and tasks pile up
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic predictions about potential disasters and a zero-tolerance belief toward mistakes, stemming from a strong burden of responsibility and low tolerance for uncertainty
target_behavior.function: Short-term relief of anxiety; seeking certainty and a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Time-consuming and inefficient, tension maintained or rebounding, still worries repeatedly after leaving the shop, with sleep and focus impaired

target_behavior.behavior: Before falling asleep at night, repeatedly worries 'whether the oven was forgotten to be turned off', finding it hard to relax and fall asleep
antecedent: When back home preparing to sleep, recalls that day's shop-closing process
target_behavior.core_reason: Excessive focus on uncontrollable consequences and emotional inference, together with the implicit assumption that 'worry equals prevention'
target_behavior.function: Trying to prevent risks and gain a sense of security through constant vigilance
target_behavior.consequence: Sleep quality declines, fatigue worsens the next day, further weakening focus and work performance
